startup.name: Surtr Defense Systems
startup.one_liner: The hardware-agnostic operating system for drone defense
startup.description: Surtr builds ParallaxOS, the open operating system for counter-UAS. It takes sensor data from any radar, RF detector, camera, or acoustic array and fuses it into a single unified picture with AI-driven threat classification and engagement recommendations. One interface, any hardware, human in the loop.

yc_acceptance.basis: Assumed accepted in this test, so this is a note. Published rate is about 1 percent of over 10,000 applicants (references/yc_acceptance.md). Two founders building defense software in a year of heavy drone and defense interest give a lift, but the description shows no defense contracts, clearances or customers.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC could pass because the counter drone software space is crowded with funded firms, the description lists no sensors integrated, defense customers or security credentials, and a two person team may not be able to sell to the Pentagon. Investors in the batch also see many counter drone pitches in 2026, so a two person team must stand out against teams that already hold prototypes, contracts or security clearances.

killers.risk: Integrated vendors beat an open hardware agnostic layer

killers.mitigation: Win integration contracts by being the neutral layer for existing sensors held by the military.

killers.risk: Long defense sales cycles and the need for clearances
killers.evidence: Defense buying runs on years and a two person team without cleared staff is slow to reach contracts.
killers.mitigation: Use SBIR and OTAs and hire a cleared advisor.

killers.risk: Crowded counter drone field with funded rivals
killers.evidence: Several YC and non YC counter drone companies compete for the same budgets.
killers.mitigation: Be the open standard that other vendors integrate with.

killers.risk: Technology risk of false alarms and classification

technical_complexity.rationale: Fusing radar, RF, camera and acoustic feeds with real time classification is demanding but feasible for strong engineers. Field tests and certifications make the full product slow to build, so a small team needs a demo with recorded data.

who: Primes such as Lockheed or RTX
